objects.description: Opaque handle type representing a CatBoost data wrapper being incrementally filled with features prior to building a DataProvider. It is managed via the C API and should be created with DataWrapperCreate and destroyed with DataWrapperDelete.

Opaque handle type representing an immutable data provider built from a DataWrapper. Constructed via BuildDataProvider. Lifetime management and destruction API is not exposed in this header; ownership and destruction details are unknown here.

Opaque handle for a loaded CatBoost model used to perform inference. Create with ModelCalcerCreate and delete with ModelCalcerDelete. After creation, load a model via LoadFullModelFromFile/Buffer/ZeroCopy before prediction. Many prediction and query functions require a valid ModelCalcerHandle.

Enumeration of prediction output types controlling post-processing of model outputs (raw value, exponent, probability, class label, RMSE with uncertainty, and multi-class probabilities). Used with SetPredictionType/SetPredictionTypeString.
Enumeration of available formula (inference) evaluator backends. Values indicate CPU or GPU evaluation. Queried via GetSupportedEvaluatorTypes and affected by EnableGPUEvaluation.

functions.name: DataWrapperCreate
functions.signature: DataWrapperHandle* DataWrapperCreate(size_t docsCount);
functions.description: Allocates and returns an empty data-wrapper for building a DataProvider with capacity for docsCount documents. Intended to be populated via Add*Features calls and then finalized with BuildDataProvider.
requirements: docsCount is the number of rows (objects) expected in all subsequent feature additions.
Returns a non-null handle on success; the handle must later be released via DataWrapperDelete.
Exact semantics of internal allocation and validation are not documented; callers should ensure all added feature arrays conform to docsCount.

functions.name: DataWrapperDelete
functions.signature: void DataWrapperDelete(DataWrapperHandle* dataWrapperHandle);
functions.description: Destroys a DataWrapper previously obtained from DataWrapperCreate and releases associated resources.
requirements: dataWrapperHandle must be a valid pointer returned by DataWrapperCreate or nullptr.
Must not be used after BuildDataProvider if ownership is transferred internally (behavior is not documented).

functions.name: AddFloatFeatures
functions.signature: void AddFloatFeatures(DataWrapperHandle* dataWrapperHandle, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize);
functions.description: Adds a block of float features to the DataWrapper. floatFeatures is an array of per-document float feature arrays; floatFeaturesSize is the number of float features per document.
requirements: dataWrapperHandle must be a valid DataWrapperHandle from DataWrapperCreate.
floatFeatures must have one entry per document (matching docsCount passed to DataWrapperCreate).
Each floatFeatures[i] must point to an array of length floatFeaturesSize.
Pointers must remain valid until BuildDataProvider is called.
Exact validation, allowed multiplicity of calls, and ownership are not documented.

functions.name: AddCatFeatures
functions.signature: void AddCatFeatures(DataWrapperHandle* dataWrapperHandle, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize);
functions.description: Adds a block of categorical features (as strings) to the DataWrapper. catFeatures is an array of per-document arrays of char* values; catFeaturesSize is the number of categorical features per document.
requirements: dataWrapperHandle must be valid.
catFeatures must have one entry per document (matching docsCount).
Each catFeatures[i] must point to an array of length catFeaturesSize of zero-terminated strings.
String pointers must remain valid until BuildDataProvider is called.
Exact validation, allowed multiplicity of calls, and ownership are not documented.

functions.name: AddTextFeatures
functions.signature: void AddTextFeatures(DataWrapperHandle* dataWrapperHandle, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize);
functions.description: Adds a block of text features (as strings) to the DataWrapper. textFeatures is an array of per-document arrays of char*; textFeaturesSize is the number of text features per document.
requirements: dataWrapperHandle must be valid.
textFeatures must have one entry per document (matching docsCount).
Each textFeatures[i] must point to an array of length textFeaturesSize of zero-terminated strings.
String pointers must remain valid until BuildDataProvider is called.
Exact validation, allowed multiplicity of calls, and ownership are not documented.

functions.name: AddEmbeddingFeatures
functions.signature: void AddEmbeddingFeatures(DataWrapperHandle* dataWrapperHandle, const float*** embeddingFeatures, size_t* embeddingDimensions, size_t embeddingFeaturesSize);
functions.description: Adds a block of embedding features to the DataWrapper. embeddingFeatures is an array (per-document) of arrays (per-feature) of float vectors; embeddingDimensions holds per-feature vector lengths; embeddingFeaturesSize is the number of embedding features per document.
requirements: dataWrapperHandle must be valid.
embeddingFeatures must have one entry per document (matching docsCount).
For each document i and embedding feature j in [0, embeddingFeaturesSize), embeddingFeatures[i][j] must point to an array of length embeddingDimensions[j].
All pointers must remain valid until BuildDataProvider is called.
Exact validation, allowed multiplicity of calls, and ownership are not documented.

functions.name: BuildDataProvider
functions.signature: DataProviderHandle* BuildDataProvider(DataWrapperHandle* dataWrapperHandle);
functions.description: Builds and returns a DataProvider from the accumulated data in the DataWrapper. Typically used to create an input data source for model evaluation.
requirements: dataWrapperHandle must be valid and previously populated via Add*Features with consistent dimensions across feature blocks.
The returned DataProviderHandle must be released via an appropriate API (not defined in this header; lifecycle management is unknown).
Post-call validity/ownership of dataWrapperHandle is not documented.

functions.name: ModelCalcerCreate
functions.signature: ModelCalcerHandle* ModelCalcerCreate();
functions.description: Allocates and returns an empty model handle used for loading and evaluating CatBoost models.
requirements: Returns a non-null handle on success; free with ModelCalcerDelete.
Must load a model (e.g., LoadFullModelFromFile/Buffer/ZeroCopy) before evaluation.

functions.name: ModelCalcerDelete
functions.signature: void ModelCalcerDelete(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle);
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a ModelCalcerHandle created by ModelCalcerCreate.
requirements: modelHandle must be a valid handle returned by ModelCalcerCreate or nullptr.
After deletion the handle must not be used.

functions.name: GetErrorString
functions.signature: const char* GetErrorString();
functions.description: Returns a thread-local pointer to the last error message (UTF-8) for the current thread, or an invalid/null pointer if no error occurred.
requirements: Returned pointer should be treated as read-only; lifetime is managed internally.
Call immediately after a function reports failure to retrieve the corresponding error.
Thread-local: only reflects errors from the calling thread.

functions.name: LoadFullModelFromFile
functions.signature: bool LoadFullModelFromFile(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, const char* filename);
functions.description: Loads a CatBoost model from a file into the given model handle.
requirements: modelHandle must be a valid handle from ModelCalcerCreate.
filename must be a valid UTF-8 path string and point to an accessible CatBoost model file.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.
On success, the handle becomes ready for evaluation.

functions.name: LoadFullModelFromBuffer
functions.signature: bool LoadFullModelFromBuffer(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, const void* binaryBuffer, size_t binaryBufferSize);
functions.description: Loads a CatBoost model from a memory buffer into the given model handle.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid.
binaryBuffer must point to a contiguous memory region of size binaryBufferSize containing the model file contents.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: LoadFullModelZeroCopy
functions.signature: bool LoadFullModelZeroCopy(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, const void* binaryBuffer, size_t binaryBufferSize);
functions.description: Maps a CatBoost model from a memory region into the model handle without copying the data.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid.
binaryBuffer must remain valid and unchanged for the entire lifetime of the model usage after this call.
binaryBufferSize must match the buffer size.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: EnableGPUEvaluation
functions.signature: bool EnableGPUEvaluation(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, int deviceId);
functions.description: Switches the evaluation backend to a specified CUDA GPU device for model evaluation.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and a model should be loaded before evaluation.
deviceId must refer to a CUDA device present in the system.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: GetSupportedEvaluatorTypes
functions.signature: bool GetSupportedEvaluatorTypes(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, enum ECatBoostApiFormulaEvaluatorType** formulaEvaluatorTypes, size_t* formulaEvaluatorTypesCount);
functions.description: Returns the list of supported formula evaluator backends for the given model handle. The function allocates an array of ECatBoostApiFormulaEvaluatorType values and sets its size.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid.
formulaEvaluatorTypes must be a valid pointer to receive an allocated array; free() must be used by the caller to deallocate it.
formulaEvaluatorTypesCount must be a valid pointer to receive the count.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: SetPredictionType
functions.signature: bool SetPredictionType(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, enum EApiPredictionType predictionType);
functions.description: Sets the prediction output type for subsequent model evaluations (e.g., raw values, probabilities, classes).
requirements: modelHandle must be valid.
predictionType must be a valid EApiPredictionType value.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: SetPredictionTypeString
functions.signature: bool SetPredictionTypeString(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, const char* predictionTypeStr);
functions.description: Sets the prediction output type using a string constant corresponding to EApiPredictionType.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid.
predictionTypeStr must be a valid zero-terminated string matching a supported prediction type.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionFlat
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionFlat(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions on flat feature vectors where all features are provided as floats. Intended for advanced users who understand CatBoost flat layout.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded with a model; desired prediction type may need to be set via SetPredictionType.
floatFeatures must have docCount entries; each entry points to an array of length floatFeaturesSize.
result must point to a buffer of size modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionFlatStaged
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionFlatStaged(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, size_t treeStart, size_t treeEnd, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Like CalcModelPredictionFlat but uses only trees in [treeStart, treeEnd) for staged evaluation.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
0 <= treeStart < treeEnd <= GetTreeCount(modelHandle).
floatFeatures/docCount/floatFeaturesSize as in CalcModelPredictionFlat.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionFlatTransposed
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionFlatTransposed(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions on a transposed dataset layout: floatFeatures is [featureIndex][docIndex]. Intended for advanced users.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
floatFeatures must have floatFeaturesSize entries (features), each entry an array of length docCount.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionFlatTransposedStaged
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionFlatTransposedStaged(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, size_t treeStart, size_t treeEnd, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Like CalcModelPredictionFlatTransposed but evaluates only trees in [treeStart, treeEnd).
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
0 <= treeStart < treeEnd <= GetTreeCount(modelHandle).
floatFeatures must have floatFeaturesSize feature arrays, each length docCount.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPrediction
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPrediction(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions using float features and string categorical features per object.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
floatFeatures: docCount entries; each array length floatFeaturesSize.
catFeatures: docCount entries; each array length catFeaturesSize of zero-terminated strings.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionStaged
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionStaged(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, size_t treeStart, size_t treeEnd, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Like CalcModelPrediction but evaluates only trees in [treeStart, treeEnd).
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
0 <= treeStart < treeEnd <= GetTreeCount(modelHandle).
floatFeatures and catFeatures dimensions as in CalcModelPrediction.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionText
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionText(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions using float, categorical string, and text string features per object.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
floatFeatures: docCount entries; length floatFeaturesSize each.
catFeatures: docCount entries; length catFeaturesSize; zero-terminated strings.
textFeatures: docCount entries; length textFeaturesSize; zero-terminated strings.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionTextStaged
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionTextStaged(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, size_t treeStart, size_t treeEnd, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Like CalcModelPredictionText but evaluates only trees in [treeStart, treeEnd).
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
0 <= treeStart < treeEnd <= GetTreeCount(modelHandle).
floatFeatures, catFeatures, textFeatures dimensions as in CalcModelPredictionText.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionTextAndEmbeddings
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionTextAndEmbeddings(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize, const float*** embeddingFeatures, size_t* embeddingDimensions, size_t embeddingFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions using float, categorical string, text string, and embedding features per object.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
floatFeatures: docCount entries; length floatFeaturesSize each.
catFeatures: docCount entries; length catFeaturesSize; zero-terminated strings.
textFeatures: docCount entries; length textFeaturesSize; zero-terminated strings.
embeddingFeatures: for each object i, an array of embeddingFeaturesSize pointers; for each embedding j, the vector length is embeddingDimensions[j].
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionTextAndEmbeddingsStaged
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionTextAndEmbeddingsStaged(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, size_t treeStart, size_t treeEnd, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize, const float*** embeddingFeatures, size_t* embeddingDimensions, size_t embeddingFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Like CalcModelPredictionTextAndEmbeddings but evaluates only trees in [treeStart, treeEnd).
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
0 <= treeStart < treeEnd <= GetTreeCount(modelHandle).
float, cat, text, and embedding features must follow the same layout rules as the non-staged variant.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionSingle
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionSingle(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, const float* floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes prediction for a single object using float and string categorical features.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
floatFeatures must point to an array of length floatFeaturesSize.
catFeatures must point to an array of length catFeaturesSize of zero-terminated strings.
result must point to a buffer of size modelApproxDimension; resultSize must equal that (1 for non-multiclass).
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionSingleStaged
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionSingleStaged(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t treeStart, size_t treeEnd, const float* floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Single-object prediction using only trees in [treeStart, treeEnd).
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
0 <= treeStart < treeEnd <= GetTreeCount(modelHandle).
float/cat features as in CalcModelPredictionSingle.
result size must equal modelApproxDimension.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionWithHashedCatFeatures
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionWithHashedCatFeatures(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const int** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);

floatFeatures: docCount entries; length floatFeaturesSize.
catFeatures: docCount entries; each array length catFeaturesSize of int hashes.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.

functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionWithHashedCatFeaturesAndTextFeatures(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const int** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);

floatFeatures: docCount entries; length floatFeaturesSize.
catFeatures (hashed): docCount entries; each array length catFeaturesSize.
textFeatures: docCount entries; each array length textFeaturesSize; zero-terminated strings.
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.

functions.name: CalcModelPredictionWithHashedCatFeaturesAndTextAndEmbeddingFeatures
functions.signature: bool CalcModelPredictionWithHashedCatFeaturesAndTextAndEmbeddingFeatures(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const int** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, const char*** textFeatures, size_t textFeaturesSize, const float*** embeddingFeatures, size_t* embeddingDimensions, size_t embeddingFeaturesSize, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions using float features, hashed categorical features, text string features, and embedding features per object.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
float/hash/text features as in the corresponding non-embedding function.
embeddingFeatures: per object, an array of embeddingFeaturesSize pointers; each embedding j length embeddingDimensions[j].
result buffer size must be modelApproxDimension * docCount; resultSize must equal that.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: PredictSpecificClassFlat
functions.signature: bool PredictSpecificClassFlat(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, int classId, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions for a specific class index using flat float features only; result contains one value per document for the requested class.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
classId must be in [0, modelApproxDimension - 1].
floatFeatures layout as in CalcModelPredictionFlat.
resultSize must equal docCount.
Returns false on error; use GetErrorString for details.

functions.name: PredictSpecificClass
functions.signature: bool PredictSpecificClass(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char*** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, int classId, double* result, size_t resultSize);
functions.description: Computes predictions for a specific class index using float and categorical string features.
requirements: modelHandle must be valid and loaded.
classId must be in [0, modelApproxDimension - 1].
floatFeatures and catFeatures layout as in CalcModelPrediction.
resultSize must equal docCount.

classId in [0, modelApproxDimension - 1].

resultSize must equal docCount.

functions.name: PredictSpecificClassSingle
functions.signature: bool PredictSpecificClassSingle(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, const float* floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const char** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, int classId, double* result, size_t resultSize);

functions.signature: bool PredictSpecificClassWithHashedCatFeatures(ModelCalcerHandle* modelHandle, size_t docCount, const float** floatFeatures, size_t floatFeaturesSize, const int** catFeatures, size_t catFeaturesSize, int classId, double* result, size_t resultSize);

data_types.description: A file containing a serialized CatBoost model in the standard CatBoost binary format. The function reads the file path (UTF-8) and loads the model by reading the file’s bytes. Any valid CatBoost model artifact produced by catboost training tools is expected.

A contiguous in-memory byte buffer holding the serialized CatBoost model in CatBoost’s binary format. The buffer contents must exactly match what would be found in a valid CatBoost model file, and size must equal the buffer length. Used for both copy-loading and zero-copy mapping of the model.

import io
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

def _leb128_u(value: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        byte = value & 0x7F
        value >>= 7
        if value:
            out.append(byte | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(byte)
            break
    return bytes(out)

# This generator crafts a plausible CatBoost native model binary. The true
# on-disk format is complex, but native format begins with a magic header and
# version fields followed by a serialized dictionary of blocks. We generate a
# minimal, internally consistent structure that many loaders accept for smoke
# paths. The goal is validity, not completeness.
#
# Structure we emit (simplified):
# [magic:"CatBoostModel\x00"]
# [version_major:u32][version_minor:u32]
# [model_format_tag:"CBM\x01"]
# [kv_count:leb128]
#   repeated kv entries:
#     [key_len:leb128][key_bytes]
#     [val_len:u32][val_bytes]
# Where values for essential keys are further structured with simple internal
# headers so the loader can parse feature counts and single tree with trivial
# leaves.
# Keys we include:
#  - "model_info": UTF-8 JSON-like text
#  - "float_features": packed list metadata (count=F)
#  - "cat_features": packed list metadata (count=C)
#  - "text_features": packed list metadata (count=T)
#  - "embedding_features": packed list metadata (count=E)
#  - "oblivious_trees": one tiny tree with depth 0 (single leaf)
#  - "approx_dimension": u32 (usually 1)
#  - "prediction_type_default": text
#  - "feature_names": joined names
# This layout is not the true format but is structurally similar enough to
# exercise loader paths that validate headers, versions, key tables and basic
# metadata without needing a real trained model.

MAGIC = b"CatBoostModel\x00"
FMT_TAG = b"CBM\x01"

def _pack_u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _pack_u64(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

def _kv(key: str, val: bytes) -> bytes:
    k = key.encode('utf-8')
    return _leb128_u(len(k)) + k + _pack_u32(len(val)) + val

def _rand_feature_names(rng: random.Random, total: int) -> List[str]:
    base = [
        "age","income","balance","clicks","views","country","device",
        "os","hour","day","user_id","item_id","price","discount",
        "query","title","text_len","emb0","emb1","emb2"
    ]
    names = []
    for i in range(total):
        if i < len(base):
            names.append(base[i])
        else:
            names.append(f"f{i}")
    rng.shuffle(names)
    return names

def _make_model(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose modest feature counts to keep size small yet exercise paths
    F = rng.randint(1, 8)          # float features
    C = rng.randint(0, 4)          # categorical features
    T = rng.randint(0, 3)          # text features
    E = rng.randint(0, 2)          # embedding features

    approx_dim = 1 if rng.random() < 0.85 else rng.choice([2, 3])

    version_major = 1
    version_minor = rng.choice([0,1,2,3])

    # model_info: emit small JSON-like blob
    info_pairs = {
        "training\_library": "catboost",
        "version": f"{version_major}.{version_minor}",
        "random_seed": str(rng.randrange(1, 1_000_000)),
        "loss_function": rng.choice(["Logloss","RMSE","MAE","MultiClass"]),
    }
    info_blob = ("{" + ", ".join(f"\"{k}\": \"{v}\"" for k, v in info_pairs.items()) + "}").encode('utf-8')

    # Feature metadata blocks: simple counts with tiny headers
    def feat_meta(count: int) -> bytes:
        # tag + count + placeholder bytes
        return b"FMTA" + _pack_u32(count) + _pack_u32(0)

    float_meta = feat_meta(F)
    cat_meta = feat_meta(C)
    text_meta = feat_meta(T)
    emb_meta = feat_meta(E)

    # Oblivious trees: single stump with one leaf vector per approx dim
    # Layout: OBT1 | tree_count(1) | depth(0) | leaf_count(1) | leaves (double)
    leaves = []
    for d in range(approx_dim):
        # produce deterministic yet varied leaf values
        val = rng.uniform(-2.0, 2.0)
        leaves.append(val)
    obt = io.BytesIO()
    obt.write(b"OBT1")
    obt.write(_pack_u32(1))          # tree_count
    obt.write(_pack_u32(0))          # depth for tree 0
    obt.write(_pack_u32(1))          # leaf_count
    # Write leaves as little-endian double array of size approx_dim
    for v in leaves:
        obt.write(struct.pack('<d', v))
    obt_blob = obt.getvalue()

    # Feature names
    names = _rand_feature_names(rng, F + C + T + E)
    feature_names_blob = ("\n".join(names)).encode('utf-8')

    # Default prediction type string
    pred_type = rng.choice(["RawFormulaVal","Probability","Class"]) if approx_dim == 1 else rng.choice(["MultiProbability","RawFormulaVal"]) 
    pred_type_blob = pred_type.encode('utf-8')

    # approx dimension as u32 with tag
    approx_dim_blob = b"ADIM" + _pack_u32(approx_dim)

    # Compose key-value table
    kv_entries = [
        _kv("model_info", info_blob),
        _kv("float_features", float_meta),
        _kv("cat_features", cat_meta),
        _kv("text_features", text_meta),
        _kv("embedding_features", emb_meta),
        _kv("approx_dimension", approx_dim_blob),
        _kv("oblivious_trees", obt_blob),
        _kv("prediction_type_default", pred_type_blob),
        _kv("feature_names", feature_names_blob),
    ]

    header = io.BytesIO()
    header.write(MAGIC)
    header.write(_pack_u32(version_major))
    header.write(_pack_u32(version_minor))
    header.write(FMT_TAG)
    header.write(_leb128_u(len(kv_entries)))

    body = b"".join(kv_entries)

    model = header.getvalue() + body
    # Keep a checksum tail to mimic some formats (optional, benign)
    checksum = sum(model) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    model += b"CHKS" + _pack_u32(checksum)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(model) > 4096:
        model = model[:4096]
    return model


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # With some probability, vary counts to generate different shapes across calls
    bump = rng.randint(0, 10)
    model = _make_model(seed ^ (bump * 0x9E3779B1))
    return model

import io
import os
import struct
import random
import zlib

# CatBoost model binary formats are proprietary and complex. For fuzzing stubs that
# call LoadFullModelFromBuffer/ZeroCopy, we need a buffer that the library is likely
# to recognize as a valid model to pass initial loading and enable deeper fuzzing.
#
# CatBoost supports exporting models to various formats. One portable and simple
# format the loader commonly accepts is a JSON model serialized as UTF-8 text.
# Many builds of CatBoost accept both the native binary and JSON textual models
# via LoadFullModelFromBuffer. While the exact field set depends on the training
# pipeline, a minimal well-formed JSON with required top-level keys and empty
# structures is often accepted for loading a stub model with zero trees.
#
# This generator therefore creates a small, valid JSON CatBoost model with:
# - Model info and metadata
# - Zero trees (empty ensemble)
# - Explicit feature counts (all zeros)
# - Minimal loss function / parameters footprint
# - Deterministic yet varied fields controlled by the seed
#
# The result stays under 2048 bytes as required by the fuzzer stub cap and under 4096.

_MIN_JSON_TEMPLATE = {
    "model_format": "CatBoostJson",
    "model_guid": "{guid}",
    "oblivious_trees": {
        "leaf_values": [],
        "tree_sizes": [],
        "tree_splits": [],
        "scale_and_bias": {"scale": 1.0, "bias": 0.0},
        "one_hot_features": [],
        "ctr_features": [],
        "float_features": [],
        "cat_features": [],
        "text_features": [],
        "embedding_features": []
    },
    "approx_dimension": {"value": 1},
    "loss_function": "RMSE",
    "params": {
        "task_type": "CPU",
        "iterations": 0,
        "border_count": 1
    },
    "feature_names": [],
    "model_info": {
        "package": "fuzz",
        "seed": "{seed}",
        "note": "minimal-zero-tree"
    }
}

# To increase coverage, we sometimes generate a tiny 1-tree model in JSON with a
# single split and two leaves. This remains valid and small while exercising more
# of the loader.

def _rand_guid(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a simple 8-4-4-4-12 hex GUID string
    def part(n):
        return ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(n))
    return f"{part(8)}-{part(4)}-{part(4)}-{part(4)}-{part(12)}"


def _json_escape(s: str) -> str:
    # Minimal JSON string escaper for inserted values
    return s.replace('\\', r'\\').replace('"', r'\"')


def _build_zero_tree_json(seed: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    guid = _rand_guid(rng)
    # Minimal deterministic structure; embed seed/guid
    # Construct JSON manually to avoid importing json and ensure stable formatting
    # and small output size.
    t = _MIN_JSON_TEMPLATE
    js = []
    js.append('{')
    js.append('"model_format":"CatBoostJson"')
    js.append(',"model_guid":"' + _json_escape(guid) + '"')
    js.append(',"oblivious_trees":{')
    js.append('"leaf_values":[]')
    js.append(',"tree_sizes":[]')
    js.append(',"tree_splits":[]')
    js.append(',"scale_and_bias":{"scale":1.0,"bias":0.0}')
    js.append(',"one_hot_features":[]')
    js.append(',"ctr_features":[]')
    js.append(',"float_features":[]')
    js.append(',"cat_features":[]')
    js.append(',"text_features":[]')
    js.append(',"embedding_features":[]')
    js.append('}')
    js.append(',"approx_dimension":{"value":1}')
    js.append(',"loss_function":"RMSE"')
    js.append(',"params":{"task_type":"CPU","iterations":0,"border_count":1}')
    js.append(',"feature_names":[]')
    js.append(',"model_info":{')
    js.append('"package":"fuzz"')
    js.append(',"seed":"' + str(seed) + '"')
    js.append(',"note":"minimal-zero-tree"')
    js.append('}')
    js.append('}')
    data = ''.join(js).encode('utf-8')
    return data


def _build_one_tree_json(seed: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a tiny 1-tree model with one float feature and two leaves.
    # CatBoost JSON schema for trees generally includes fields like tree_sizes,
    # leaf_values, and tree_splits encoding splits. Keep consistent sizes.
    guid = _rand_guid(rng)
    # Choose a threshold and leaf values deterministically but varied
    thr = round(rng.uniform(-2.0, 2.0), 6)
    left = round(rng.uniform(-1.0, 0.0), 6)
    right = round(rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0), 6)
    # tree_sizes: [1] (one split)
    # leaf_values: 2 values for a depth-1 oblivious tree
    # tree_splits: minimal description; in CatBoost JSON this is usually an array of
    # objects with split metadata. Some loaders accept simplified entries. We'll
    # provide a compact representation CatBoost commonly writes.

    js = []
    a = js.append
    a('{')
    a('"model_format":"CatBoostJson"')
    a(',"model_guid":"' + _json_escape(guid) + '"')
    a(',"oblivious_trees":{')
    a('"tree_sizes":[1]')
    a(',"leaf_values":[' + str(left) + ',' + str(right) + ']')
    # Minimal split description: float feature index 0 with threshold
    a(',"tree_splits":[{"split_type":"FloatFeature","float_feature_index":0,"border":' + str(thr) + '}]')
    a(',"scale_and_bias":{"scale":1.0,"bias":0.0}')
    a(',"one_hot_features":[]')
    a(',"ctr_features":[]')
    a(',"float_features":[{"feature_index":0,"flat_feature_index":0,"border_count":1,"nan_value_treatment":"AsIs","has_nans":false}]')
    a(',"cat_features":[]')
    a(',"text_features":[]')
    a(',"embedding_features":[]')
    a('}')
    a(',"approx_dimension":{"value":1}')
    a(',"loss_function":"RMSE"')
    a(',"params":{"task_type":"CPU","iterations":1,"border_count":1}')
    a(',"feature_names":["f0"]')
    a(',"model_info":{')
    a('"package":"fuzz"')
    a(',"seed":"' + str(seed) + '"')
    a(',"note":"minimal-one-tree"')
    a('}')
    a('}')
    return ''.join(js).encode('utf-8')


def _maybe_wrap_as_cbm(json_bytes: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Some loaders auto-detect JSON vs binary. Keep as pure JSON most of the time.
    # Occasionally gzip-compress and prepend a simple marker commonly recognized by
    # loaders that support compressed model content (e.g., when reading from files).
    # We keep it plain here to maximize acceptance via buffer loaders.
    return json_bytes


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose between zero-tree and one-tree to exercise different code paths
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        blob = _build_zero_tree_json(seed, rng)
    else:
        blob = _build_one_tree_json(seed, rng)

    # Ensure size within fuzzer bound
    if len(blob) > 2048:
        blob = blob[:2048]
    return blob
